keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «그래도 전기차는 완벽한 해결책이 아니다(한계)» 와 «전기차는 깨끗한 교통으로 가는 중요한 한 걸음이지만, 더 큰 계획의 일부일 때 가장 효과적이다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the limit (electric cars are not a perfect solution) and the conclusion (electric cars are an important step but work best as part of a bigger plan). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: No exhaust while driving and lower running costs

qs.q: Why were electric cars pushed off the road in the early 1900s?
qs.qko: 1900년대 초에 전기차가 도로에서 밀려난 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Cheap oil and mass-produced gasoline cars became common
Electric cars were too noisy for cities
evs: However, cheap oil and mass-produced gasoline cars soon pushed them off the road.
In the late 1800s and early 1900s, electric cars were popular in cities because they were quiet, clean, and easy to drive.
Drivers also worry about charging time and the number of charging stations.
Lithium-ion batteries became much cheaper over the past decade, which made longer driving ranges possible.
why: 본문에 값싼 석유와 대량 생산된 휘발유 차가 곧 전기차를 도로에서 밀어냈다고 나와요.
The text says cheap oil and mass-produced gasoline cars soon pushed electric cars off the road.

qs.q: In the text, what does "cheaper to run" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «cheaper to run» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: It costs less to drive them, since electricity often costs less than gasoline
They are cheaper to buy than any other car
They can run faster than gasoline cars
evs: They can also be cheaper to run, since electricity often costs less than gasoline for the same distance.
Lithium-ion batteries became much cheaper over the past decade, which made longer driving ranges possible.
Many governments have also offered subsidies and set future limits on new gasoline car sales.
In the late 1800s and early 1900s, electric cars were popular in cities because they were quiet, clean, and easy to drive.
why: «cheaper to run» 은 «운행하는 데 돈이 덜 든다» 는 뜻이에요. 같은 거리를 갈 때 전기가 휘발유보다 싼 경우가 많다고 설명해요.
It means they cost less to drive, because electricity often costs less than gasoline for the same distance.

qs.q: Why might an electric car not be very clean in some places?
qs.qko: 어떤 곳에서는 전기차가 그다지 깨끗하지 않을 수 있는 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Its power may come from coal, and mining battery materials can harm the environment
It produces thick exhaust while driving
It needs gasoline to start its engine
evs: Their environmental benefit depends on how the electricity is produced, and power from coal is far less clean than power from solar or wind.
Making batteries requires mining materials such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel, which can harm the environment and workers.
Because EVs produce no exhaust while driving, they can improve air quality in crowded cities.
As a result, global EV sales rose quickly, and Korean companies became major producers of both cars and batteries.
why: 전기를 석탄으로 만들면 훨씬 덜 깨끗하고, 배터리 재료를 캐는 일이 환경과 노동자에게 해를 줄 수 있어요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
Power from coal is far less clean, and mining battery materials can harm the environment and workers. You need both sentences.

ends: How are old electric car batteries recycled?

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «If» 뒤에는 «누가 + 무엇을 바꾸면» 을, «we can» 뒤에는 동사원형으로 시작하는 결과를 써 보세요. (예: If we take the bus, we can reduce traffic)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «If», write who changes what; after «we can», start with a base verb. (e.g. If we take the bus, we can reduce traffic)
